answer: Trust propagates through bounded random walks on the attestation graph, so influence depends on paths that repeatedly reach independently trusted regions, not merely on the number of identities. A sybil cluster—even one labeled hollow, timber, or zenith—has limited voting weight when its sparse external cut gives it low conductance: few edges let the walk escape. Conductance bounds the cluster’s share of stationary flow, constraining aggregate influence unless it earns substantial external attestations.
